a.clean: Chapter 4 of the book club handbook covers how to choose a book. The first step is to collect suggestions, and every member is allowed to propose up to two titles. After that, the organizer compiles a shortlist of no more than six and circulates it a week before the vote. Voting is by ranked choice, which means each member lists their top three, and the winner is the title with the most points. In the case of a tie, the member who hosted most recently had the casting vote. Members should keep in mind that books over 400 pages need extra time, so the organizer may schedule them for a two-month slot.

b.clean: Okay, story time because you will not believe what happened at the front desk this morning. A guy walks up at 6 a.m., completely soaked, no luggage, and says he's checking in under the name of his brother, who is apparently already in a row. I said, sir, I can't give you a key without ID, he said, fine, I'll go get him, and he disappears. Twenty minutes later he comes back with his brother, who is in a bathrobe and also wet, and it turns out they'd both fallen in the fountain outside. Long story short, we gave them towels and a free breakfast and now they've booked another night. The manager was thrilled.

We're currently running with four vacancies on the nursing side, and two of the agency nurses have given notice, which Agnes and I think is going to put us under real pressure by the end of the quarter. We've interviewed six candidates so far and made offers to three, one of whom has already accepted. I'd like to propose that we extend the overtime approval until the end of November. That would cost roughly £8,000 a month, but it's cheaper than the agency rates. I've attached the figures. Please let me know if you'd like to discuss before the board meeting on the 3rd. Kind regards, Cursed Boker
